To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C allele at position ABCC4 4976 was associated with beta-2-microglobuluria in HIV-1-infected patients receiving tenofovir-containing antiretrovirals.
the allele frequency of the ABCC gene was associated with the development of beta2-micoglobulinuria.
approximately 20% of patients receiving TDF had elevated levels of beta2-MG in urine, and the C allele at position T4976 of the ABCB4 gene was associated significantly with beta2-MGuria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a single-nucleotide-polymorphism in ABBC4, which is associated with beta2-Microglobulinaemia in Thai patients with HIV-1 infection.
the development of a new method to detect and quantify the levels of beta2 microglobulin in urine samples.
the study of a new polymorphism in the ABCC4 protein which is associated with the risk of developing TDF-related kidney damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study is an important first step in the identification of genetic factors that influence TDF-associated KID in Thai HIV-1 infected individuals, but further research is required to confirm and extend these findings.
this study found an association between a single-nucleotide-polymorphism in the ABCC4 and beta2-microglo-bulinuria in patients receiving TDF for at least one-year.
the ABCC4 T-4976C polymorphism is associated with tenofoviral induced beta2-microglubulinuria in Thai patients infected with HIV-1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C allele at position T4976 of the ABC transporter ABCC4 gene is associated with beta2 microglobulinuria in TDF-treated HIV-infected patients.
ABCC4 polymorphism is associated with beta2 microglobulinuria in patients receiving TDF, which might be a marker for TDF-induced kidney dysfunction.
the C allele at position of ABCC4 gene may help to identify the patients at greater risk of TDF-associated KDT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ABCC4 polymorphism is associated with tenofovr-induced beta2-microgloobulinuria.
the C allele at position T4976C of the ABCC 4 gene is associated with beta2 microglobulinuria in patients with HIV infection receiving TDF.

we have found a genetic marker that is associated with the development of Tenofovir-associated kidney dysfunction, and that marker is a single nucleotide polymorphism in the ABCC4 transporter gene, which is located on chromosome 4.
